holidays.name: Halloween
holidays.greeting: Happy Halloween from MuskegMan Photography! Tonight the porches glow, the costumes come out, and every doorway becomes a portrait studio — if you know how to work the dark.
tips: Expose for the flame: jack-o'-lanterns want 1/15–1/30s, f/2–4, ISO 400–800 — porch light OFF.
Portraits by porch light: wide open f/1.8–2.8, spot-meter on the face, not the dark background.
Skip the flash — it flattens the mood. Raise the ISO and let the shadows do the talking.

challenge.title: The Halloween Glow Hunt
challenge.goal: Capture the night without killing it: a glowing jack-o'-lantern or a costume portrait lit only by porch light, candle or string lights — no flash allowed. 3 shots.

holidays.name: Thanksgiving
holidays.greeting: Happy Thanksgiving from MuskegMan Photography! The best food-photography light of the year is a kitchen window — and the best candids happen while everyone thinks you're not shooting.
tips: Shoot the spread near a window: soft side light, and plates +1 EV so white dishes read white, not gray.
Kitchen candids: 1/125s or faster, auto ISO, and stay wide — 35mm keeps the story in frame.
Group shots: f/5.6–f/8 so every face is sharp, and use the 2-second timer — get IN the photo.

holidays.name: Christmas
holidays.greeting: Merry Christmas from MuskegMan Photography! This is bokeh season — the one week a year the whole world hangs up tiny lights for you. Here's how to make them sing.
tips: Tree bokeh: focus on your subject wide open (f/1.4–f/2) and the tree melts into glowing orbs.
Shooting the tree itself: ISO 800–1600, 1/30s braced, WB Tungsten ≈3500K — and no flash.
Morning chaos: auto ISO with a 1/125s floor so wrapping-paper moments stay sharp.

holidays.name: New Year
holidays.greeting: Happy New Year from MuskegMan Photography! Sparklers, fireworks and a countdown — the most photogenic night of the year. Tripods at the ready.
tips: Sparkler writing: tripod, f/4–5.6, ISO 100–200, 2–6 seconds per letter — someone writes, you shoot.
Fireworks: f/8–16, 2–6s, ISO 100 — shoot the burst, check the screen, adjust, repeat.
Countdown candids: 1/125s+, ISO 1600–3200 — shoot wide and shoot a lot, the joy is in the faces.

holidays.name: Valentine's Day
holidays.greeting: Happy Valentine's from MuskegMan Photography! Candlelight, string lights, and one person who doesn't mind the camera — let's make something worth printing.
tips: Candlelit portrait: f/1.8–2.8, ISO 800–1600, 1/60s — bring the candle close, one light is enough.
String-light bokeh: subject 6+ feet in front of the lights, wide open, focus on the eyes.
The roses: side window light and a dark background — flowers love it as much as faces do.

holidays.name: Easter
holidays.greeting: Happy Easter from MuskegMan Photography! Spring light, pastels, and a backyard egg hunt — the fastest action sport in photography is a 5-year-old who just spotted the last egg.
tips: Egg hunt: 1/500s+, continuous focus and burst mode — kneel down to kid eye level.
Pastels on overcast days: the clouds are a giant softbox, no flash needed.
Spring blooms: f/2.8–4 and watch the background — a busy bush fights the subject.

holidays.name: Mother's Day
holidays.greeting: Happy Mother's Day from MuskegMan Photography! The best gift is a photograph she's actually in — and hand someone else the camera today too, so Mom gets a picture WITH everyone.
tips: Window-light portrait: face the window, f/2–2.8, +0.3 EV — soft, flattering, free.
The flowers she got: overcast light and a plain background beat any filter.
Generations shot: open shade, f/5.6+, and shoot 10 frames — someone always blinks.

holidays.name: Independence Day
holidays.greeting: Happy Independence Day from MuskegMan Photography! Fireworks are the year's easiest 'wow' — tripod, low ISO, and let the shutter run long.
tips: Fireworks: tripod, f/8–16, ISO 100, 2–6s per burst — arrive early, frame wide, shoot the finale manually.
Sparkler portraits: 1/60s, f/2.8–4, ISO 800 — the sparkler is a warm little lamp.
Backyard BBQ: 1/250s for game action, and shoot the flag against the sky.
